Decision — site URL layout

Status: accepted 2026-10-16, after review by two independent reviewers.

The question

mixos.dev serves two readers from the same files. A person in a browser gets a static HTML page, and nothing needs JavaScript to render. An agent or script on any machine fetches the same page as Markdown and starts from /llms.txt. MixOS will grow to hundreds of apps, services, libraries and tools over the next few years. How should the URL space be organised, so that an address, once published, never has to change?

The decision

Two namespaces

  • Each component's documentation is at the top level, under the component's name. Examples: /mix/, /term/, /compd/, /hostd/, /noded/.
  • Everything that is not a component lives under /docs/. That covers guides such as /docs/try/ and /docs/drive/, plus /docs/decisions/, /docs/spec/, /docs/dev/, /docs/releases/, and the generated indexes below. The site's global navigation has a Docs entry that leads there.

Component names

  • A component's name is the component declared by its principal package in [package.metadata.mixos], or by its component.mx. Component names are already plain, unique across the workspace and never reused (see source layout), so an address can be built from the name alone.
  • A component name starts with a lowercase letter and contains only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
  • Two names are reserved: docs and v. The component metadata gate refuses them, so a forbidden name is caught when the component is created, not when the site is built.
  • Site machinery uses names no component can take. Generator inputs and assets live in _build/ and _web/ (renamed from build/ and web/), and root files (index.html, 404.html, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, CNAME, the favicons) all contain a dot or start with an underscore.
  • Mix's names. The mix component is the language library, so /mix/ is the Mix language manual and the same pages mix man TOPIC reads. The mix binary's component is system (/system/), and the shell is mix-shell (/mix-shell/). Each links to the others.

Where pages come from, and their addresses

The path of a source file relative to the site root (the repository's docs/ directory) determines its address. The table gives every mapping:

SourceHTMLMarkdown
docs/<name>/README.md/<name>//<name>/README.md
docs/<name>/<page>.md/<name>/<page>//<name>/<page>.md
docs/docs/<page>.md/docs/<page>//docs/<page>.md
<component dir>/CHANGELOG.md (mirrored)/<name>/changelog//<name>/changelog.md
Generated index pages/docs/<index>//docs/<index>.md
  • The Markdown is published at its source path. Relative links inside it therefore resolve correctly under ordinary URL resolution. An agent builds a component's Markdown address as /<name>/README.md. The generator checks every relative link in both formats.
  • Hand-written component documentation lives in docs/<name>/. That is its one canonical copy. The component's own directory keeps a short README.md that points to the page, so someone browsing the source finds it.
  • CHANGELOG.md stays beside the code, where releases update it. Only the principal package's changelog is published. The published copy is generated and never edited. Relative links in it are rewritten to the source on GitHub. A component with no changelog has no changelog page. changelog is therefore a reserved page name inside every component.
  • The doubled docs/docs/ is accepted. It keeps the rule that the source path determines the address, without a rename table.
  • Generated pages have a Markdown twin like every other page.
  • HTML is the canonical address. Each HTML page names its Markdown as <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">. sitemap.xml lists HTML only.

Navigation from metadata

  • The URL never encodes kind, layer or install profile. These change over a component's life: a library is promoted, or a desktop service becomes useful headless.
  • /docs/desktop/ and /docs/server/ are generated index pages listing components by their declared install profiles. A component in both is listed in both, with one page. Components in the base profile are listed under a reader-facing heading such as "Core components". The word base stays in the installation docs.
  • /docs/components/ is the one complete, generated component index, giving each component's name, kind, profiles, source path and page. It replaces the hand-run docs/docs/dev/components.md (formerly docs/dev/components.md).
  • Until profiles is declared everywhere, the indexes list undeclared components as unclassified. They never guess from layer.

Agents

  • /llms.txt lists every section, with absolute Markdown URLs: one line per component (with its kind and profiles) and one per page under /docs/. Every published document can be reached from it. llms-full.txt remains an optional single file.
  • Every page states that it describes the current main branch.

Every component has a page

  • The principal package of every component (app, service, cli or lib) and every Mix component must have docs/<name>/README.md. Private crates and tool and test packages are excluded.
  • A component without a page fails the site gate. While existing components are being documented, the ones still missing are named in an exception list in site.conf.mix. That list may only shrink, and a new component cannot be added to it.

Addresses are permanent

From the day this decision is accepted:

  • A profile change or a source move never changes an address.
  • An address that goes away keeps working in both formats: an entry in site.conf.mix's redirects for browsers, plus a short Markdown page at the old .md address that names the new one, because an agent fetching Markdown does not follow an HTML redirect.
  • A split leaves a page that links to its successors. A retired component keeps a retirement page, which stays listed in /llms.txt, and its name is never reused.

Versions

/v/ is reserved for versioned copies of the site. How they work is decided before the first stable release.

Why

  • One namespace for components, one for everything else. An address either names a component or starts with /docs/. Only two names are off limits for components.
  • Names are the most stable thing a component has. The source-layout decision rejected splitting the source tree by desktop, server or core, because a component could plausibly sit in either of two places and moves between them. Putting that axis into URLs would have recreated the problem where a move is most costly.
  • It matches what already works. /mix/ and the existing component pages (/hostd/, /noded/, /prefs/, /backdrop/, /screenshot/, /dopus/) are already at the top level, and mix man already fetches /mix/<topic>.md and /mix/README.md.
  • One canonical copy. Keeping hand-written docs in docs/ rather than beside the code relaxes the source-layout principle that a component is self-contained. That is deliberate: documentation for readers has one home, one navigation and one gate. Code, tests and changelogs stay with the component.

Rejected

  • Mirror repository paths (/apps/term/, /libs/bus/). The address is predictable, but it encodes kind, and it moves when a component moves in the source tree.
  • Sections by install profile (/desktop/term/, /server/maild/, /base/noded/). Profiles are deployment data that change, a component can be in two, and server is empty today. A profile change would move a public URL.
  • A component prefix (/c/term/ or /components/term/). It protects the component namespace, but /docs/ does the same job from the other side, with shorter, more readable component URLs.
  • Docs beside the code, mirrored into the site. That makes two copies, needs a freshness gate and a mapping table, and splits navigation.
  • A /<name>.md alias for each component page. Relative links in it would resolve against the wrong directory.
  • Mapping /docs/ to a differently named source directory (for example docs/guides/). It avoids docs/docs/, but it adds a permanent rename table.

Consequences

  • Nobody depends on the current URLs, so this one move keeps no old address. The permanence rules apply from acceptance.
  • The root pages that are not components move under docs/docs/: try and drive, plus decisions/, spec/ and dev/.
  • Root pages that describe a component become its page (docs/hostd.md becomes docs/hostd/README.md, and so on). Four were named after a topic rather than their component, and take the component's name: edit becomes editd, portal becomes portald, bridge becomes bridged and releases becomes releasesd. (The first draft of this record listed edit, bridge and releases as non-component pages; each documents one service.)
  • The component READMEs beside the code move into docs/<name>/README.md, leaving a pointer behind. The CHANGELOGs stay where they are.
  • docs/build/ and docs/web/ become docs/_build/ and docs/_web/.
  • The component metadata gate gains the name grammar and the reserved names.
  • gen-site gains the output-collision check (every HTML, Markdown, asset and generated output), the changelog mirror, the generated indexes and their Markdown twins, the alternate links, the missing-page gate with its exception list, and a grouped llms.txt.
  • Every link to a moved page is updated, including in AGENTS.md and the decision records.
